safety_scope: General wellness and self-reflection only. Do not use these practices to override genuine safety measures, protective boundaries, accessibility aids, medication or professional instructions, urgent action, or qualified advice.

practices.title: Test Your Prediction
best_used_when: the feared outcome is specific enough to observe
a small ordinary-risk test or observation is available
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
the action is irreversible or unusually high stakes
practices.micro_action: Write one prediction, one safe observation, and one result.
practices.prompt: Turn one anxious prediction into something observable, then compare it with what actually happens.
practices.reflection_question: What changed, if anything, about how certain you are?

practices.title: Problem or Worry?
best_used_when: you can state the concern clearly enough to ask whether a practical action exists
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
you would use hypothetical to dismiss a concrete problem you could reasonably act on
practices.micro_action: Classify one concern and either schedule one action or park it for review.
practices.prompt: Ask whether this concern has a practical next action or is mainly a future-focused what-if.
practices.reflection_question: Did more thinking create a usable action, or another version of the same what-if?

practices.title: Spot the Safety Behavior
best_used_when: the situation is objectively low risk
the behavior is not a genuine safety requirement
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
you are unsure whether the behavior is protective in the real world
practices.micro_action: Identify one possible safety-seeking behavior; change nothing until real safety is clear.
practices.prompt: Name one extra behavior used mainly to prevent anxiety or embarrassment, then check whether it is genuinely protective.
practices.reflection_question: What did the behavior prevent you from learning?

practices.title: Park and Return
best_used_when: you can choose a realistic later review point
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
delaying action would materially worsen a concrete problem
practices.micro_action: Write it once and choose when you will review it.
practices.prompt: Capture the worry once, choose a later review point, and return to the current task without requiring the worry to disappear.
practices.reflection_question: Did postponing create space, or was there a real action that should not have been delayed?

practices.title: Reflection or Replay?
best_used_when: you have already identified the main facts and any usable lesson
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
you are still missing information needed for a concrete decision or accountability step
practices.micro_action: Ask: what new information did the last round produce?
practices.prompt: Check whether another minute of analysis is producing a new fact, decision, or action. If not, end the review deliberately.
practices.reflection_question: Did stopping avoid a real task, or simply stop repetition?

practices.title: One Less Check
best_used_when: the situation is ordinary and objectively low risk
the extra check is non-essential and not required
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
the check prevents a plausible material harm
practices.micro_action: Skip one clearly non-essential check in an ordinary low-risk situation.
practices.prompt: In a low-risk situation, choose one clearly non-essential check or reassurance request to skip and observe the uncertainty without replacing it.
practices.reflection_question: What happened to the outcome, and what happened to the urge for certainty?

practices.title: The Smallest Approach Step
best_used_when: a smaller first step can be defined
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
avoidance is serving a legitimate protective boundary or recovery need
practices.micro_action: Take one safe approach step small enough to finish now.
practices.prompt: Shrink a safe avoided task until you can approach one observable part without making completion the goal.
practices.reflection_question: What did you learn from approaching that planning alone could not show?

practices.title: Set the Good-Enough Contract
best_used_when: the task has discretionary quality rather than a mandated exact standard
you can define fit-for-purpose criteria before more checking
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
the work has a legitimately strict safety, compliance, accuracy, or professional standard
practices.micro_action: Write three completion criteria before doing another pass.
practices.prompt: Define the minimum fit-for-purpose criteria before the next round of work, then stop when those criteria are met unless new evidence appears.
practices.reflection_question: Did extra work improve the required outcome or mainly reduce discomfort about stopping?

practices.title: Use a Continuum, Not a Verdict
best_used_when: you are evaluating quality, progress, or performance that can reasonably vary by degree
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
the situation truly has a binary safety/compliance requirement
practices.micro_action: Rate one result on two specific dimensions instead of success/failure.
practices.prompt: Replace a total success/failure verdict with a 0–10 description of specific dimensions.
practices.reflection_question: What becomes visible when the result is not forced into one total verdict?

practices.title: Describe the Behavior, Not the Identity
best_used_when: a specific behavior, choice, or skill can be named
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
the reframing would erase responsibility or harm that needs repair
practices.micro_action: Turn one identity label into one specific behavior statement.
practices.prompt: Translate a global label about yourself into a specific, reviewable description of what happened and what can change.
practices.reflection_question: Does the specific version preserve responsibility while making change more possible?

practices.title: Run the Same-Standard Check
best_used_when: the comparison person is in genuinely similar circumstances
you want to test whether the rule changes only because it is you
avoid_when: genuine danger or urgent safety issue
required safety, professional, legal, or accessibility rule
medical, legal, financial, or safeguarding decision
the roles, duties, risks, or prior commitments are materially different
practices.micro_action: Write the self-rule and same-situation rule for someone else.
practices.prompt: Compare the standard you use for yourself with the standard you would use for another person in the same role and circumstances.
practices.reflection_question: Is the difference explained by real responsibility or only by who is judged?
